Variants are the pricing question

Star Wars Unlimited prints cards in multiple treatments, and hyperspace and showcase versions sit above the standard printing of the same card. Foil runs add a further split.

Card AI suggests records with the set and card number. Review the artwork and confirm the variant and finish before using that printing's price.

Leaders and bases behave differently from the main set

Leader and base cards have their own demand curve, driven by competitive play as much as by collecting. They are recorded as distinct entries so their value is visible rather than buried in a collection total.

Raw and graded copies kept apart

Raw cards are stored with condition, graded cards with grading company and grade. The same card can be held as both, each valued on its own market.

Star Wars Unlimited card scanner questions.

Can Card AI identify hyperspace variants?

The scan suggests catalog matches. Review the artwork and confirm hyperspace, showcase or standard treatment before adding the card.

Does it track foil Star Wars Unlimited cards separately?

Yes. Finish is recorded per card, so foil and non-foil copies are separate entries with their own prices.

Can I track it alongside other card games?

Yes. Star Wars Unlimited and other supported games can share one collection with a single total value.

Can I check values without scanning each card?

Yes. Search the database to check star wars unlimited card value directly, and the cards you add become a star wars unlimited collection tracker that revalues as the market moves.
